Briefing for 10 November 2026

Short items for 10 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

New model

Claude Fable 5.2: faster and 20% cheaper

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 for all users and Mythos 5.2 for verified security and life-science groups. Both share one model, run up to 30% faster than 5.1 and cost $8 per million input tokens.

Source: Anthropic

New model

Meta's Muse Ember targets everyday agent work

Meta calls Muse Ember its smallest and most efficient model, built for tool calls, coding subtasks, routing and long documents. Meta claims more intelligence per dollar than Claude Haiku 5.5 or GPT-6 Luna.

Source: The Verge

New model · More technical

NVIDIA GR00T 2 learns robot skills from human video

At the CoRL robotics conference, NVIDIA presented GR00T 2, an open robot foundation model built on Cosmos. It predicts video and robot actions together and can pick up fine skills from videos of people.

Source: NVIDIA

Everyday tool

Disney and Adobe build custom generative AI models

In a multi-year deal announced at Adobe MAX, the two firms will train artist-led models on Disney's own characters and styles using Firefly Foundry, for parks, cruises, studio work and ESPN.

Source: Adobe

Device

Telekom doubles the chips in its Munich AI factory

The first stage was fully booked after seven months, so Deutsche Telekom is adding NVIDIA B300 systems and growing the site to 20 megawatts. It is investing almost another quarter billion euros.

Source: Deutsche Telekom

Everyday tool

German job agency: AI cuts and creates 800,000 jobs

Andrea Nahles, head of Germany's Federal Employment Agency, expects about 800,000 jobs to disappear due to AI over 15 years, with a similar number of new ones. Business services, banks and insurers are hit harder.

Source: Handelsblatt

Device

Anthropic reportedly buys $3.4B in gas generators

According to the Financial Times, Anthropic took over existing orders for gas generators with 1.7 gigawatts of capacity to power future data centers. Power supply has become a key bottleneck for AI growth.

Source: TechCrunch

Be brave. Get smart.
